quick.summary: Why rerunning a failed job sometimes doubles your numbers, and how to fix it.
quick.takeaway: Design jobs so they wipe existing data for that period before adding more.

beats.line: My job failed halfway. I ran it again, and now totals are doubled. Why?
Because your code added the same items twice.
Think of an elevator button. Pushing it ten times does not call ten elevators.
It just makes sure one elevator is coming.
Right. We call this an idempotent operation.
Can I just say safe to repeat?
I like that better. Safe to repeat.
Your pipeline should clear out the old attempt before adding anything new.
So if it breaks, I can just hit run again safely.
And you will never double count a sale again.

quiz.question: What does it mean for a pipeline to be safe to repeat?
options: Running it multiple times produces the same final result as running it once.
It never crashes or shows any errors.
It backs up the entire database before every run.
It asks for a password before it starts.
quiz.explanation: A repeatable job handles mistakes smoothly. If you trigger it twice, it will not duplicate your records.

quiz.question: A safe pipeline simply appends all new records blindly to the bottom of the table.
quiz.explanation: Blindly appending causes duplicates on a rerun. You should drop or overwrite the existing batch first.
